findings.title: Whole collection results are processed synchronously on the UI isolate
findings.source: User: AGENTS.md:39-44; software-design skill sections 3-4 on ownership and section 11 on concrete structural evidence.
findings.trigger: A refresh discovers many collections or reads a collection with many matching children, now permitted beyond the previous 1000-collection and 2000-child limits.
findings.evidence_kind: Static source inspection; no runtime reproduction or timing measurement.

where.children: Completed results for up to eight collections; each result contains every returned page.
where.indexed: Pairs each result with its zero-based position.
where.index: The result's position within the collection batch.
where.page.items: All matching child records accumulated for that collection, not one 200-item response.
where.result: The request-local map from item identifiers to collection names.
where.putIfAbsent: Obtains the existing names list or creates an empty list.
where.batch[index].value: The name of the collection corresponding to this result.

evidence.ownership: CatalogController calls client.catalog before its worker handoff. Transport offloads sufficiently large JSON decoding, but returns decoded maps to the caller. _collectionItems accumulates all pages, after which _collections traverses complete discovery and child lists on the UI isolate.
evidence.scale: The accepted count limit permits up to one million records per listing. A completed eight-collection batch can therefore require millions of synchronous map operations. Network page size does not bound this final traversal.
evidence.maintenance_cost: The apparent 200-item request bound hides a separate whole-list CPU bound. Changes to paging capacity must also account for discovery reduction and membership reduction.
evidence.ticket_search: No dedicated follow-up recording this collection-processing issue was found. The closed ta-7oe6 ticket covers library-entry construction and explicitly retains collection names in the returned payload.

findings.impact: Large refreshes can monopolize the isolate responsible for drawing frames and handling input. The exact delay is unmeasured. This finding does not explain tf-il7u.
findings.remedy: Move large collection-result reduction off the UI isolate without changing refresh cadence or retained-worker ownership. Alternatively, use the explicit allowance in AGENTS.md:39: record a dedicated follow-up ticket and link it from this ticket and its evidence before integration. A broader redesign is not required for this review resolution.
